questions.q: Water is conveyed through a uniform tube of 8 $\mathrm{cm}$ in diameter and $3140 \mathrm{~m}$ in length at the rate $2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^3$ per second. The pressure required in maintain the flow is (Viscosity of water $=10^{-3}$ SI units)
questions.solution:
Radius $r=\frac{8}{2} \mathrm{~cm}=4 \mathrm{~cm}=4 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}$,
Rate of flow of water
$\begin{aligned} & Q=2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^3 / \mathrm{s} \\ & Q=\frac{\pi P r^2}{8 \eta l}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad P=\frac{Q(8 \eta l)}{\pi r^4}\eta=$ coefficient of viscosity of water $=10^{-3}$ SI units
$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad P & =\frac{2 \times 10^{-3} \times 8 \times 10^{-3} \times 3140}{3.14 \times\left(4 \times 10^{-2}\right)^4} \\ & =\frac{2 \times 8 \times 3140 \times 10^{-6}}{3.14 \times 256 \times 10^{-8}} \\ & =\frac{3140 \times 10^2}{3.14 \times 16} \\ & \left.=\frac{100 \times 10^3}{16}\right] \\ & =6.25 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Consider a vessel filled with a liquid upto height $H .$ The bottom of the vessel lies in the $X - Y$ plane passing through the origin. The density of the liquid varies with $Z$-axis as $ρ \left(z\right) = {ρ}_{0}  \left[$2 - $\$left(\dfrac{z}{H}\right)$2\right]$. If ${P}_{1}$ and ${P}_{2}$ are the pressures at the bottom surface and top surface of the liquid, the magnitude of  \left({P}_{1} - {P}_{2}\right)$is :
questions.solution:
Given that, $P \left(Z\right) = {ρ}_{0} \left($2 - $\$left(\dfrac{Z}{H}\right)$2\right)$

Let a small column of liquid thickness be $dz$.

Pressure due to column,

$d{P}_{1} = {ρ}_{0} \left( \left($2 - \dfrac{Z}{H}\right)2\right]gdz + {P}_{2}$

${P}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{π}{ρ}_{0}\left($2 - $\$left(\dfrac{Z}{H}\right)2\right)gdz + {P}_{2}$

$= {ρ}_{0}g{∫}_{0}^{π}\left($2 - \dfrac{Z2}{H2}\right)dz + {P}_{2}^{'}$

$= {ρ}_{0}g\left($2H - \dfrac{1}{3H^{2}}\left(H^{3}\right)\right) + {P}_{2}$

${P}_{1} = {ρ}_{0}g\left($2H - \dfrac{H}{3}\right) + {P}_{2}$

${P}_{1} - {P}_{2} = {ρ}_{0}g\dfrac{5H}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3}{ρ}_{0}gH$

$

questions.q: On heating water, bubbles beings formed at the bottom of the vessel detach and rise. Take the bubbles to be spheres of radius $R$ and making a circular contact of radius $r$ with the bottom of the vessel. If $r < < R$ and the surface tension of water is $T$,~value of $r$ just before bubbles detach is (density of water is $ρ$)
questions.solution:
Forces acting on the bubble are:

\left(a\right)$~Buoyant force in upward direction

$B = {ρ}_{w}Vg$

$⇒ B = {ρ}_{w}\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}g \ldots \left(1\right)$,

where,~${ρ}_{w} =$density of water.

\left(b\right)$~Force due to surface tension.

If we consider an elemental length~$dl$~at bottom contact, then force due to surface tension is~$dF = Tdl$~along the tangent to surface & perpendicular to~$dl .$

Clearly~$dFcos\theta$~components on two diametrically elements cancel out &~$dFsin\theta$~components add up.

$∴$~Net force due to surface tensions on the bubble

$F = ∫ dFsin \theta = {∫}_{0}^{2\pir}Tdl\dfrac{r}{R}$

$⇒ F = \dfrac{Tr}{R}2\pir = \dfrac{2\piTr^{2}}{R} \ldots \left(2\right)$

When the bubble is on the verge of detaching then

$B = F$

$⇒ {ρ}_{w}\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}$g = \dfrac{2\piTr^{2}}{R}$

$⇒ r = R^{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}\dfrac{{ρ}_{w}g}{T}}

questions.q: A stream of water flowing horizontally with a speed of $15ms^{- 1}$ gushes out of a tube of cross-sectional area ${10}^{- 2}m^{2}$ and hits a vertical wall nearby. The force exerted on the wall by the impact of water (assuming it does not rebound) is
questions.solution:
If the velocity of the stream be $v$ (say) . In $\text{1 second}$ , the distance travelled $= v .$

$∴$ The volume of water hitting the wall per second, $V = va$

Where, $\text{a}$ is the cross-sectional area.

$⇒ V = 15m / s \times {10}^{- 2}m^{2}$

[ $∴$ Given, $v = 15m/s, a = {10}^{- 2}m^{2}$ ]

$⇒ V = 15 \times {10}^{- 2}m^{3} / s$

Mass of water hitting the wall per second,

$m = volume \times Density$

$= 15 \times {10}^{- 2} \times {10}^{3}$

$= 150kg / s$

[$∵$ Density of water $= 1000kg / m^{3}$ ]

Initial momentum of the water hitting the wall per second $= m \times v$

$= 150 \times 15$

$= 2250{kgm / s}^{2}$

$= 2250N$

Final momentum per second $= 0$

$∴$ Force exerted on the wall = Change in the momentum of water stream per second

$= 2250N$

$= 2.25 \times {10}^{3}N$

questions.q: Two soap bubbles combine to form a single bubble. In this process, the change in volume and surface area are respectively $V$ and $A$. If $P$ is the atmospheric pressure, and $T$ is the surface tension of the soap solution, the following relation is true :
questions.solution:
Let radii of two soap bubbles are $a$ and $b$ respectively and radius of single larger bubble is $c$.
As excess pressure for a soap bubble is $\frac{4 T}{r}$ and external pressure $P$.
$P_i=P+\frac{4 T}{r}$
So, $\quad P_a=P+\frac{4 T}{a}, P_b=P+\frac{4 T}{b}$
and $\quad P_c=P+\frac{4 T}{c}$ ...(i)
and $\quad V_a=\frac{4}{3} \pi a^3, \quad V_b=\frac{4}{3} \pi b^3$
and $\quad V_c=\frac{4}{3} \pi c^3$ ...(ii)
Now as mass is conserved.
$\mu_a+\mu_b=\mu_c$
i.e., $\quad \frac{P_a V_a}{R T_a}+\frac{P_b V_b}{R T_b}=\frac{P_c V_c}{R T_c} \quad($ as $P V=\mu R T)$
As temperature is constant, i.e., $T_a=T_b=T_c$
So, $\quad P_a V_a+P_b V_b=P_c V_c$
which in the light of Eqs. (i) and (ii) becomes,  \left(P+\frac{4 T}{a}\right)$\$left(\frac{4}{3} \pia^3\right)+ $\$left(P+\frac{4 T}{b}\right)\$left(\frac{4}{3} \pib^3\right)= \$lleft(P+\frac{4 T}{c}\right) $\$left(\frac{4}{3} \pic^3\right)$
i.e., $4 T \left(a²+b²-c²\right)=P  \left($c^3-a³-b³\right)$ ...(iii)
Now, $\quad V=\frac{4}{3} \pi  \left($a^3+b³-c³\right)$ and $\quad A=4 $\pi\left($a^2+b²-c²\right)\therefore \quad \frac{T A}{\pi}=-\frac{3}{4 \pi}V P$
or $\quad 4 T A+3 P V=0$

questions.q: A tank of height $H$ is fully filled with water. If the water rushing from a hole made in the tank below the free surface, strikes the floor at a maximum horizontal distance, then the depth of the hole from the free surface must be
questions.solution:
As hole is made in the tank below the free surface of water, so water rushing from this hole follows a parabolic path.

The velocity of efflux liquid,

$v = \sqrt{2gh}$

Time, $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\left(H - h\right)}{g}}$

Horizontal range, $R = vt$

$R = \left(2gh \times \dfrac{2 \left($H - h\right)}{g}\right)\dfrac{1}{2}$

$ie, R^{2} = $4h \left($H - h\right) = $4\left($Hh - h^{2}\right)$

The range is maximum if

\dfrac{dR}{dh} =$0$

or\dfrac{2RdR}{dh} =$4 \left($H - 2h\right)$

$or0 = \left($H - 2h\right)$

$orh = $\dfrac{H}{2}$

questions.q: For a concrete sphere of radius $R$ having a cavity of radius $r$ packed with sawdust, to float with its entire volume submerged under water what will be the ratio of mass of concrete to mass of sawdust? Given the specific gravities of concrete and sawdust are respectively $2.4$ and $0.3$.
questions.solution:
Let specific gravities of concrete and sawdust are $ρ{}_{1}$ and $ρ{}_{2}$ respectively.
According to principle of floatation, weight of whole sphere = upthrust on the sphere

$\dfrac{4}{3} \pi \left(R^{3} - r^{3}\right) {ρ}_{1} \text{g} + \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^{3} {ρ}_{2} \text{g} = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^{3} \times 1 \times \text{g}$

$⇒ {\text{R}}^{3} {ρ}_{1} - r^{3} {ρ}_{1} + r^{3} {ρ}_{2} = R^{3}$

$⇒ R^{3} \left({ρ}_{1} - 1\right) = r^{3} \left({ρ}_{1} - {ρ}_{2}\right) ⇒ \dfrac{R^{3}}{r^{3}} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{1} - {ρ}_{2}}{{ρ}_{1} - 1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{R^{3} - r^{3}}{r^{3}} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{1} - {ρ}_{2} - {ρ}_{1} + 1}{{ρ}_{1} - 1} ⇒ \dfrac{\left(R^{3} - r^{3}\right) {ρ}_{1}}{r^{3} {ρ}_{2}} = ( \dfrac{1 - {ρ}_{2}}{{ρ}_{1} - 1} ) \dfrac{{ρ}_{1}}{{ρ}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\text{Mass of concrete}}{\text{Mass of saw dust}} = ( \dfrac{1 - 0 \text{.} 3}{2 \text{.} 4 - 1} ) \times \dfrac{2 \text{.} 4}{\text{0} \text{.} 3} = 4$

questions.q: A cubical block of side $10$ cm floats at the interface of oil and water. The pressure above that of the atmosphere at the lower face of the block is
questions.solution:
We know that the& absolute pressure at a depth& $h$~in a liquid of density~$ρ$~is given as

$P = {P}_{0} + hρg$

where~${P}_{0} =$~Atmospheric pressure.

Therefore, the pressure at~the lower face of the block

$P = {P}_{0} + {ρ}_{1}g{h}_{1} + {ρ}_{2}g{h}_{2}$

$⇒ P - {P}_{0} = {ρ}_{1}g{h}_{1} + {ρ}_{2}g{h}_{2}$

$⇒ ∆ P = \left(600\right) \left($10\$right)\left($0 . 1\right) + \left(1000\$right)\left(10\right)\left($0 . 02\right)$

$⇒ ∆ P = 800Nm^{- 2}$

$

questions.q: A layer of oil with density $724kgm^{- 3}$ floats on water of density $1000kgm^{- 3}$. A block floats on the oil-water interface with $1/6$ of its volume in oil and $5/6$ of its volume in water, as shown in the figure. What is the density of the block?
questions.solution:
Given,
Density of oil \left({ρ}_{1}\right) = 724kg / m^{3}$
Density of water \left({ρ}_{2}\right) = 1000kg / m^{3}$

According to Archimedes' principle,

Up thrust = Weight of the liquid displaced

$⇒ {Vρ}_{b}g = {V}_{o}{ρ}_{1}g + {V}_{w}{ρ}_{2}g$ (${V}_{o}$ and ${V}_{w}$ are volumes of oil and water displaced respectively)

${Vρ}_{b}g = \dfrac{V}{6}\left(724\right)g + \dfrac{5V}{6}\left(1000\right)g$, where ${ρ}_{b}$=density of block.

and, ${V}_{o} = \dfrac{V}{6}$ and ${V}_{w} = \dfrac{5V}{6}$

$⇒ {Vρ}_{b}g = \left(\dfrac{724V}{6} + \dfrac{5000V}{6}\right)g$
$⇒ {Vρ}_{b}g = \left(\dfrac{724V + 5000V}{6}\right)g$
$⇒ {Vρ}_{b}g = \dfrac{5724}{6}Vg$

${ρ}_{b} = 954kg / m^{3}$

To find the point of action of total force, y_R=$\frac{I_{x c}}{y_c A}+$y_c where, $y_R=$ location where point of force acts, $A=$ area, $y_c=$ location where total weight acts $=h / 2$ and $I_{x c}=$ moment of inertia (here rectangular plate). =$\frac{1}{12}$A h²=$\frac{1}{12}$b h³ So, $\begin{aligned}$y_R \text{ and } =$\frac{(1 / 12) b h^3}{(1 / 2) h \cdot b h}+\frac{1}{2}$h \\ \text{ and } =$\frac{1}{6}$h+$\frac{1}{2}$h=$\frac{2}{3}$h \end{aligned} (from the top) So, $y_R=\frac{h}{3}$ (above the base $)=\frac{2}{3} h$ (from the top $)$

questions.q: A liquid kept in a cylindrical vessel is rotated about vertical axis through the centre of circular base. The difference in the heights of the liquid at the centre of vessel and its edge is $(\mathrm{R}=$ radius of vessel, $\omega=$ angular velocity of rotation, $\mathrm{g}=$ acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution: When the cylindrical vessel is rotated at angular speed $\omega$ about its axis, the velocity of the liquid at the sides is maximum, given by $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{s}}=\mathrm{r} \omega$ Applying Bernoulli's theorem at the sides and at the center of the vessel, we have $\mathrm{P}+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrmv^{2}=$ constant $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{s}}+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{s}}^{2}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{c}}+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{c}}{ }^{2}$ where $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{s}}=$ pressure at the sides $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{s}}=$ velocity of the liquid at the sides $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{c}}=$ pressure at the center $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{c}}=$ velocity of the liquid at the center $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{c}}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{s}}=\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{s}}^{2}=\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrmr^{2} \omega^{2} \ldots(\mathrm{I}) \quad \because \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{c}}=0$ Since $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{c}}$ is greater than $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{s}}$, the liquid rises at the sides of the vessel. Let $\mathrm{h}$ be the difference in the levels of the liquids at the sides and at the center, so we have $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{c}}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{s}}=\rho g h \ldots(\mathrm{II})$ from (I) and (II) we have $\rho g h=\frac{1}{2} \rho r^{2} \omega^{2}\Rightarrow h=\frac{r^{2} \omega^{2}}{2 g}$
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main

questions.q: A metal plate of the area& $500{cm}^{2}$ is kept on a horizontal surface with a layer of oil of thickness~$0 . 5mm$ between them. The horizontal force required to drag the plate with a velocity of~$2cms^{- 1}$ is (coefficient of viscosity$= 0 . 9kgm^{- 1}s^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
Here, we have to find out the horizontal force required to drag the plate kept on the metal surface& since the fluid is viscous. Hence, the required force should be the viscous force,
\left|F\right| = ηA\dfrac{dV}{dx}$~where~$η$~is coefficient of viscosity,~$A$~is the cross-section area and~$\dfrac{dV}{dx}$~is the rate of shear deformation.
$⇒ F = 0 . 9 \times 500 \times {10}^{- 4} \times \left(2 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)\left($0 . 5 $\times {10}^{- 3}\right)

$⇒ F = 0 . 9 $\times$2 = 1 . 8N$

A small orifice is opened at some height in the cylinder and the water level is reduced to height of orifice in $20 \mathrm{~s}$. Height of water in vesse $=1 \mathrm{~m}$ Let orifice is at a depth $h$ from above
Time taken to reduce the water level up to orifice, t=$\frac{A}{A_0} \sqrt{\frac{2 x}{g}}$where, $A_0=$ area of orifice and $A=$ base area. $\text { Given, } \begin{gathered} \frac{A}{A_0}=$100, t=20 $\mathrm{~s} \Rightarrow$20=100 $\sqrt{\frac{2 x}{10}}$\\ $\sqrt{\frac{x}{5}}=\frac{1}{5} \Rightarrow$x=$\frac{1}{5}=$0.2 $\mathrm{~m} \text { or }$20 $\mathrm{~cm} \end{gathered}$Now, height of orifice from base, h=100-20=80 $\mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: Two objects suspended from the arms of a balance are in equilibrium when completely submerged in water. The mass of one body is $36g$ and its density is $9g{cm}^{- 3}$. If the mass of the other object is $48g$, then its density in $g{cm}^{- 3}$ is
questions.solution:
Apparent weight $= \text{V} \left(ρ - \sigma\right) \text{g} = \dfrac{\text{m}}{ρ} \left(ρ - \sigma\right) \text{g}$

where m = mass of the body, $ρ$ = density of the body and $\sigma$ = density of water If two bodies are in equilibrium then their apparent weight must be equal.

$∴ \dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{ρ}_{1}} \left({ρ}_{1} - \sigma\right) \text{g} = \dfrac{{m}_{2}}{{ρ}_{2}} \left({ρ}_{2} - \sigma\right) \text{g}$

$⇒ \dfrac{3 6}{\text{9}} \left(9 - 1\right) = \dfrac{4 8}{{ρ}_{2}} \left({ρ}_{2} - 1\right) \text{g} \text{.}$

By solving we get ${ρ}_{2} = 3$ .

questions.q: Under isothermal conditions, two soap bubbles of radii ' $r_1$ ' and ' $r_2$ ' combine to forms a single soap bubble of radius ' $R$ '. The surface tension of soap solution is ( $\mathrm{P}=$ outside pressure)
questions.solution: Pressure inside the first bubble $=\mathrm{P}+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_1}$ Pressure inside the second bubble $=\mathrm{P}+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_2}$ Using the formula $\mathrm{PV}=\mathrm{nR} \theta \quad(\theta=$ absolute temp $)\left(\mathrm{P}+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_1}\right) \cdot \frac{4 \pi}{3} \mathrm{r}_1^3=\mathrm{n}_1 \mathrm{R} \theta \quad$ ( $\mathrm{R}$ is molar gas constant) \left(\mathrm{P}+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_2}\right) \cdot \frac{4 \pi}{3} \mathrm{r}_2^3=\mathrm{n}_2 \mathrm{R} \theta$ and \left(\mathrm{P}+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}}\right) \cdot \frac{4 \pi}{3} \mathrm{R}^3=\left(\mathrm{n}_1+\mathrm{n}_2\right) \mathrm{R} \theta\therefore\left(\mathrm{P}+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}}\right) \cdot \frac{4 \pi}{3} \mathrm{R}^3=\left(\mathrm{P}+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_1}\right) \cdot \frac{4 \pi}{3} \mathrm{r}_1^3+\left(\mathrm{P}+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_2}\right) \cdot \frac{4 \pi \mathrm{r}_2^3}{3}\therefore\left(\mathrm{P}+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}}\right) \mathrm{R}^3=\left(\mathrm{P}+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_1}\right) \mathrm{r}_1^3+\left(\mathrm{P}+\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_2}\right) \mathrm{r}_2^3$ on solving: $\mathrm{T}=\frac{\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{R}^3-\mathrm{r}_1^3-\mathrm{r}_2^3\right)}{4\left(\mathrm{r}_1^2+\mathrm{r}_2^2-\mathrm{R}^2\right)}$

questions.q: A water tank kept on the ground has an orifice of $2 \mathrm{~mm}$ diameter on the vertical side. What is the minimum height of the water above the orifice for which the output flow of water is found to be turbulent? (Assume, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2, \rho_{\text {water }}=10^3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$, viscosity $=1$ centi-poise)
questions.solution: Here, $D=2 \mathrm{~mm}, \eta=1$ centi-poise $=10^{-3} \mathrm{~Pa}-\mathrm{s}$ and density of the water, $\rho=10^3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ For flow to be just turbulent, $R_e=3000$ \therefore \quad v=$\frac{R_e \eta}{\rho D}=\frac{3000 \times 10^{-3}}{10^3 \times 2 \times 10^{-3}}=$1.5 We know that the velocity head, $h=\frac{v^2}{2 g}$ \Rightarrow \quad h=$\frac{(1.5)^2}{2 \times 10}=$0.1125 \simeq 11 $\mathrm{~cm}$So, no option is matched.

$

The free body diagram of block + tube inclusive of water is as shown. Since the block + tube system shown in figure is in equilibrium.

questions.q: If the work done in blowing a bubble of volume $V$ is $W$, then the work done in blowing the bubble of volume $2V$ from the same soap solution will be
questions.solution:
As volume of the bubble

v$= \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^{3} ⇒ \text{R} = {\left(\dfrac{3}{4 \pi}\right)}^{1 / 3} V^{1 / 3} ⇒ R^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{3}{4 \pi}\right)}^{2 / 4} V^{2 / 3}$

$⇒ R^{2} \alpha V^{2 / 3}$

Work done in blowing a soap bubble

$\text{W} = 8 \pi R^{2} \text{T} ⇒ \text{W} ∝ R^{2} ∝ V^{2 / 3}$

$∴ \dfrac{{W}_{2}}{{W}_{1}} = {\left(\dfrac{{V}_{2}}{{V}_{1}}\right)}^{2 / 3} = {\left(\dfrac{2 \text{V}}{\text{V}}\right)}^{2 / 3} = {\left(2\right)}^{2 / 3} = {\left(4\right)}^{1 / 3} ⇒ {W}_{2} = 4 3 \text{W}$

questions.solution:
Given that, \left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \operatorname{rd}$ part of body is above the water surface.
$\therefore$ Volume of body outside the water $=\frac{1}{3}$(volume of body) $V_o=\frac{1}{3} V\therefore$ Volume of body inside, $V_i=V-V_0=V-\frac{V}{3}=\frac{2 V}{3}$ Let mass of body $=M$ Density of body $=\sigma$ Density of water, $\rho=10^3 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$ According to the law of floatation, body will float into the liquid (water) when weight of body is balanced by Buoyant force. $\therefore \quad W=F_B\Rightarrow \quad M g=V_i \rho g\begin{gathered}V \sigma g=V_i \rho g \\ V \sigma=V_i \rho \\ \sigma=\frac{V_i \rho}{V}\end{gathered}$ Substituting the values, we get $\begin{aligned} \sigma & =\frac{2 V}{3 V} \rho \\ & =\frac{2}{3} \times 10^3=\frac{2000}{3} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}\end{aligned}$ Hence, density of liquid, $\sigma=\frac{2000}{3} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}

questions.q: A cylindrical tank with a large diameter is filled with water. Water drains out through a hole at a bottom of the tank. If the cross-sectional area of the hole is $6{cm}^{2}$ then the drainage rate~  \left(m^{3}s^{- 1}\right)$~when the depth of the water is $0 . 2m$, is$
questions.solution:
Applying the Bernoulli equation,

${p}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{1}^{2} + ρg{h}_{1} = {p}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{2}^{2} + ρg{h}_{2}$

Here,~ the height of the water in the tank is ${h}_{1}$,

${p}_{1}$ is the pressure of water in the tank, and

${v}_{1}$ is the~velocity of the water.~

${h}_{2}$ is the hole's height,

${p}_{2}$ is the pressure at hole, and

${v}_{2}$ is the water's pace at the hole and~

$ρ$~represents~the water density.

There acts the same atmospheric~pressure at the top of the tank and at the hole, thus& ${p}_{1} = {p}_{2}$.

We will neglect the water velocity at the top since the tank is large as its velocity is much smaller than the velocity at the hole.

Now, the Bernoulli equation becomes,~$ρg{h}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{2}^{2} + ρg{h}_{2}$

$⇒ {v}_{2} = \sqrt{2g\left({h}_{1} - {h}_{2}\right)}$

$⇒ {v}_{2} = \sqrt{2 \times 9 . 81 \times \left(0 . 2\right)} = 1 . 98ms^{- 1}$

The drainage rate is~${A}_{2}{v}_{2} = 6 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 1 . 98$

$⇒ {A}_{2}{v}_{2} = 1 . 18 \times {10}^{- 3} = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 3}m^{3}s^{- 1}$

questions.solution: The force balance invovles, surface-tension force and boyancy force balance the weight of the droplet, so the equation is: $(2 \pi r) T+\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3\right) \mathrm{dg}=\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3\right) \mathrm{Qg}$ Where, $\mathrm{r}$ is the radius of the drop, $\mathrm{T}$ the interfacial tension between the liquids, $g$ is acceleration due to gravity. Therefore, $\mathrm{T}=\left(\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{r}^2\right)(\mathrm{Q}-\mathrm{d}) \mathrm{g}$ Diameter $=2 r=\left[\frac{6 T}{g(Q-d)}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}$.

(i)] $=4 \$piR^2\left($n^{1 / 3}-1\right)$ The work done for change in area, $W=T $\times \Delta$A=T \times4 \piR^2  \left($n^{1 / 3}-1\right)$ This work is store in the form of energy.

questions.q: Water flows out of a big tank along a tube bent at right angles; the inside radius of the tube is equal to $r = 0 . 50cm$. The length of the horizontal section of the tube is equal to $l = 22cm$. The water flow rate is $Q = 0 . 50Ls^{- 1}$. Find the moment of reaction forces of flowing water, acting on the tube's walls, relative to the point $Q$.
questions.solution:
Consider only bend part of the tube.

The change in momentum of mass Δm of liquid as it passes through the bend,





$\Delta \overset{→}{P} = \overset{→}{P}f ⁡ - \overset{→}{P}i ⁡ = \Delta m ⁡ v ⁡ \overset{^}{i} - \Delta m ⁡ v ⁡ \left(- \overset{^}{j}\right) = \Delta m ⁡ v ⁡ \overset{^}{i} + \Delta m ⁡ v ⁡ \overset{^}{j}$

∴ $\overset{→}{F} = \dfrac{\Delta P ⁡}{\Delta t} = v ⁡ \dfrac{\Delta m ⁡}{\Delta t} \overset{^}{i} + v ⁡ \dfrac{\Delta m ⁡}{\Delta t} \overset{^}{j}$

$= v ⁡ \left(ρS ⁡ \dfrac{\Delta L ⁡}{\Delta t}\right)\overset{^}{i} + v ⁡ \left(ρS ⁡ \dfrac{\Delta L ⁡}{\Delta t}\right)\overset{^}{j ⁡} = ρS ⁡ v{⁡}^{2}\overset{^}{i} + ρS ⁡ v{⁡}^{2}\overset{^}{j}$

∴ Reaction force on the tube at bend point is ${\overset{→}{F}}_{0} = - \overset{→}{F}$

∴ $\overset{→}{F}0 = - ρS ⁡ v{⁡}^{2}\overset{^}{i ⁡} - ρS ⁡ v{⁡}^{2}\overset{^}{j} = - ρ\pir{⁡}^{2}v{⁡}^{2}\overset{^}{i} - ρ\pir{⁡}^{2}v{⁡}^{2}\overset{^}{j}$

Moment of the force $\overset{→}{F}0\text{about}O ⁡$ is
$\overset{→}{N} = \overset{→}{l} \times {\overset{→}{F}}_{0} = \left(l ⁡ \overset{^}{i}\right) \times \left\{- ρ \pi {r ⁡}^{2} {v ⁡}^{2} \overset{^}{i} - ρ \pi {r ⁡}^{2} {v ⁡}^{2} \overset{^}{j}\right\}$
$\overset{→}{N} = - ρ \pi {r ⁡}^{2} {v ⁡}^{2} l ⁡ \overset{^}{k}$

∴ \left|\overset{→}{N}\right| = ρ \pi {r ⁡}^{2} {v ⁡}^{2} l ⁡$

$\text{But}\text{Q} = \text{Sv}$

∴ $v ⁡ = \dfrac{Q ⁡}{S ⁡} = \dfrac{Q ⁡}{\pir{⁡}^{2}}$

$∴ \overset{→}{\text{N}} = ρ\pir^{2}l ⁡ \left(\dfrac{Q ⁡}{\pir{⁡}^{2}}\right)2 = \dfrac{ρQ{⁡}^{2}l ⁡}{\pir{⁡}^{2}}$

$

Time taken for the level to fall from $H$ to $H^{'}$ is given by

$\text{t} = \dfrac{\text{A}}{{A}_{0}} \sqrt{\dfrac{\text{2}}{\text{g}}} \left[\sqrt{\text{H}} - \sqrt{H^{′}}\right]

According to problem the time taken for the level to fall from $h$ to \dfrac{\text{h}}{2}

${t}_{1} = $\dfrac{\text{A}}{{A}_{0}} \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{\text{g}}} [ \sqrt{\text{h}} - \sqrt{\dfrac{\text{h}}{2}} ]

Similarly, time taken for water level to fall from \dfrac{h}{2} to $0$ is

${t}_{2} = $\dfrac{\text{A}}{{A}_{0}} \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{\text{g}}} [ \sqrt{\dfrac{\text{h}}{2}} -$0 ]$

$∴ $\dfrac{{t}_{1}}{{t}_{2}} = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - 0} = \sqrt{2} -$1

questions.q: A cubical block of wood having mass of $160 \mathrm{~g}$ has a metal piece fastened underneath as shown in the figure. Find the maximum mass of the metal piece which will allow the block to float in water. Specific gravity of wood is 0.8 and that metal is 10 and density of water $=1 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cc}$.
questions.solution: Volume of wood block $=\frac{\text { Mass }}{\text { Density }}=\frac{160}{0.8 \times 1}=\frac{1600}{8}=200 \mathrm{~cm}^3$ Let mass of metal piece is $x \mathrm{~g}$. $\text { Volume of metal piece }=\frac{\text { Mass }}{\text { Density }}=\frac{x}{10 \times 1}=\frac{x}{10} \mathrm{~cm}^3$ Total volume of fluid displaced $=\left(200+\frac{x}{10}\right) \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~m}^3$ Weight of fluid displaced $=V \times \rho_f \times g=\left(200+\frac{x}{10}\right) 10^{-6} \times 1000 \times 10=\left(200+\frac{x}{10}\right) 10^{-2} \mathrm{~N}$ If block floats in water, then weight $=$ upthrust $\Rightarrow(160+x) 10 \times 10^{-3}=\left(200+\frac{x}{10}\right) \times 10^{-2}160+x=200+\frac{x}{10}\frac{9 x}{10}=40x=\frac{400}{9}=44.4 \mathrm{~g}$
